newsitem.title: INDIA: India approves Telecom Regulatory Authority.
newsitem.headline: India approves Telecom Regulatory Authority.

text.p: The Indian cabinet on Wednesday approved the creation of the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI), which is empowered to regulate the telecommunications industry, the government said.
"The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India would be a statutory and high-powered body with a substantial measure of autonomy," the government said in a statement.
The TRAI would regulate the telecommunications industry, particularly basic telephone services, which India opened up to the private sector under an economic reform programme launched in 1991.

The government had introduced a bill in parliament last year to set up the TRAI, but withdrew it after criticism from opposition lawmakers who said the body did not have sufficient independence to regulate the telecommunication industry.
The issue was later considered by a parliamentary committee. Officials said the committee's views were considered by the cabinet, which approved the TRAI with enhanced powers and autonomy.
"It is hoped that the authority would become operational at an early date after consideration and passing of the bill in parliament," the government said in a statement.

Private firms that won licences to set up telephone services had earlier expressed fears that it may be difficult for them to compete with the state-run Department of Telecommunications without the presence of a strong and independent regulator.
"The TRAI will be a body consisting of a chairperson and members belonging to various disciplines such as telecommunications, finance, law and consumer affairs," the government statement said.

The regulator will resolve disputes between telephone service companies, ensure technical compatibility and inter-connectivity between them, regulate tariffs and protect consumer interests and competition, the statement said.
